reasoning_traces.think:
E-processes form a family of martingales that allow anytime-valid inference without pre-specifying sample size. They are constructed such that the probability of rejecting a true null hypothesis remains bounded by a significance level α. This is achieved by defining a supermartingale M_t where M_0 = 1 and M_t ≥ 0 for all t. The key insight is that if we observe data up to time t and define a stopping rule based on M_t, then the probability of incorrectly rejecting H₀ is controlled. In GSI, this translates to real-time hypothesis testing using e-processes as confidence sequences. Log-odds pooling aggregates predictions from multiple models into a single calibrated estimate. It leverages the fact that log-odds are additive under independence, allowing for aggregation of model outputs. By applying extremization, the system can correct for miscalibration while maintaining diversity among ensemble members. This mechanism is essential for sim-to-real calibration in GSE. Kelly betting provides an optimal strategy for maximizing logarithmic wealth when the edge is known. Its formulation f* = (bp − q)/b balances expected gain against risk. In practice, fractional Kelly is preferred due to estimation uncertainty and conservatism. For GSE, this translates into dynamic stake allocation that adapts to changing market conditions and estimated edges.
